changed.from: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) has exactly one \(L\)-Lipschitz representative \(g_{t,P}\) on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), so \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)\) exists uniquely. Consequently \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. Consistency implies that \(g_{t,P}\) is also compatible, \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere, with a version of \(z\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=z]\); this supplies the potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point.
changed.to:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.
changed.reason: The current claim is false on the declared class. The smoothness assumption controls the regression only inside the closed \(h_0\)-tube, so outside that tube the support may contain positive-mass points whose regression values violate every global Lipschitz bound. The core also neither states that \(\mathcal A_0\) is the complement of \(\mathcal A_1\) nor imposes integrability on an unobserved counterfactual away from its assigned side; those omissions prevent the asserted full-support potential-outcome conditional mean from being well defined and identified. The proposed claim restricts uniqueness and compatibility to the near-boundary region actually controlled by the assumptions, which is sufficient to identify both traces, and gives the usual full-side local conclusion under an explicit partition condition.

changed.reason: Two restrictions are necessary. First, the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) equals zero at \(n=1\), while the nontrivial Gaussian regression class has positive minimax risk, so the frontier is necessarily for sufficiently large \(n\). Second, sharp assignment defines treatment through \(\mathcal A_1\), whereas the estimators average observations indexed by \(\mathcal A_t\); without \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), the control-side average need not use untreated observations.

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses none of \(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For arbitrary slack lower and upper profile envelopes the two displayed bounds need not coincide, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.

\[

\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).

{"id":"thm:arbitrary-modulus-two-sided-bracket","kind":"theorem","statement":"Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the finite one-sided score measure
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t).
\]
If \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(r>0\), put \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\).  Positivity of \(m\) and \(\mathrm{ass:declared\text{-}modulus\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\), which is a member property in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\), imply
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,s)
 \ge m(s)>0. \tag{40}
\]
Thus \(x\) belongs to \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\) for both sides.  The member property \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) makes the specified representative continuous at \(x\), so the definition of the trace gives
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{41}
\]
Because \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), the sharp-assignment member property makes \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T_i=t\).  Hence, conditionally on the scores, the mean of every observed side average is the corresponding average of \(g_{t,P}(X_i)\).  The bounded-trace member property gives \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\).  Euclidean projection onto that interval is nonexpansive relative to every point of the interval; therefore clipping cannot increase the pointwise error, and the clipped pointwise loss is at most \(4L\).

We first prove the upper bound.  Fix \(h\) such that \(h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\) and
\[
 nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h). \tag{42}
\]
Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_K\) be a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\).  Maximality makes it an \(h\)-net, since otherwise one could add an uncovered boundary point.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) gives \(K\le C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), for each \(j,t\),
\[
 N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\sim\operatorname{Bin}\{n,q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\},
 \qquad q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\ge m(h). \tag{43}
\]
For \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\), followed by \(1-y\le e^{-y}\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{N\le nq/2\}
 &\le 2^{nq/2}\mathbb E(2^{-N})
 =2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n\\
 &\le\exp\{nq(\log 2-1)/2\}
 \le e^{-nq/8}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{44}
\]
Let \(H_h\) be the event that \(N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\ge nm(h)/2\) for every \(j\) and \(t\).  Equations (43)--(44) and the union bound imply
\[
 \Pr_P(H_h^c)\le2C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. \tag{45}
\]
For any \(x\in\mathcal B\), choose \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le h\).  Since \(B(z_j,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\), on \(H_h\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)
 \ge\frac{nm(h)}2. \tag{46}
\]
Choose the fixed constant \(A\) large enough that (42) makes the right side of (46) at least \(8\log(e+n/(2h))\).  Then \(2h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(H_h\), by \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}bandwidths}\).

Condition on \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\).  For any nonempty averaging set indexed by \((x,b,t)\), (41) and the Lipschitz member property give the deterministic bias bound
\[
 \left|
 \frac{1}{N_{t,n}(x,b)}
 \sum_{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le b}g_{t,P}(X_i)
 -\theta_{t,P}(x)
 \right|\le Lb. \tag{47}
\]
Let \(Z_n\) be the maximum normalized error over the nonempty disk patterns in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), with that lemma's zero convention if there is no pattern.  The exact conditional Gaussian condition in \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), routed through that lemma, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)
 \le
 \sqrt{2\log\!\left\{4|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^{3}\binom nj\right\}}+1
 \le C\sqrt{\log(e+n)}. \tag{48}
\]
On \(H_h\), every selected bandwidth is admissible and its averaging set is nonempty.  Conditional on the scores, the selected bandwidth is fixed because it depends only on the counts.  Equations (47)--(48), \(b\le h_0<1\), and \(\log(e+n)\le\log(e+n/b)\) show that the conditional expected error of a selected side fit is bounded by a constant times its criterion in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\).  The minimizing property of that definition and the admissible comparison bandwidth \(2h\), together with (46), therefore give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \mathrel{\Big|}X_1,\ldots,X_n
 \right]
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 \quad\text{on }H_h. \tag{49}
\]
Here the two side errors were added; the fixed numerical factors caused by \(2h\) and (46) are absorbed into \(C\).

Projection does not enlarge the error.  On \(H_h^c\), its supremum is at most \(4L\).  Taking expectations in (49) and using (45) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}
 |\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\\
 &\qquad\le C\left\{Lh+\sigma
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 +CLh^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{50}
\]
After increasing \(A\) to at least a fixed numerical constant, (42) implies
\[
 h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}
 \le h^{-1}(e+n/h)^{-A/8}
 \le h
\]
up to a constant depending only on \(h_0\).  Thus the last term of (50) is absorbed by \(CLh\).  Independently of (42), the clipped loss is at most \(4L\).  Taking the infimum over every qualifying dyadic pair, with the prescribed empty-set convention, proves the upper display.  The maps in \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}counts}\), \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\), \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}bandwidths}\), \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), and \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\), followed by fixed projection, use neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\).

We next prove the lower display inside the same class.  Choose a law \(P^\circ\) in the assumed nonempty class and retain its score marginal and assignment geometry.  On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), define \(P_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\).  Every score-dependent member property is unchanged.  The side regressions and traces are zero, so the Lipschitz, trace-envelope, Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency properties in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\) all hold.  Hence
\[
 P_0\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}). \tag{51}
\]

\[
 \min_{t\in\{0,1\}}q_{t,P_0}(x_j,h)\le u.
\]

\[

 \qquad

\]

Thus the regression smoothness and trace envelope remain valid; all design conditions are unchanged, and the residual about the shifted observed conditional mean is still \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\).  Consequently
\[
 P_j\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
 \qquad 1\le j\le M. \tag{53}
\]
Equation (40) puts every center in both side supports.  The sign in the construction ensures that, whether \(t_j=0\) or \(t_j=1\), the causal contrast at \(x_j\) increases by \(\eta_h\).  For \(k\ne j\), \(d(x_j,x_k)\ge h\), whereas \(\psi_{k,h}\) is supported on \(B(x_k,h/3)\), so \(\psi_{k,h}(x_j)=0\).  Therefore
\[

\]

\[
 \log\frac{\phi_\sigma(y-\mu)}{\phi_\sigma(y)}
 =\frac{\mu y}{\sigma^2}-\frac{\mu^2}{2\sigma^2},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{Y\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)}
 \log\frac{\phi_\sigma(Y-\mu)}{\phi_\sigma(Y)}
 =\frac{\mu^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{55}
\]
The perturbation is present only when \(X\in\mathcal A_{t_j}\), and its tent is supported inside \(B(x_j,h/3)\subseteq B(x_j,h)\).  By (55), independent sampling, and \(q_{t_j,P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\),
\[

 &\le\frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}.

\]

\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}

\[
\mathcal C_n(x)=\left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
\widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
satisfies, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\),
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.

\mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge
\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
\left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the exact conditional Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
The fallback event obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\},
\]
and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.  Consequently, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \asymp (\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
In particular, uniformly over \(\mathcal P_\kappa^{\mathrm{perv}}\), \(\mathbb E_P\sup_x W_n(x)\le C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus the frozen assumptions yield an explicit honest global band and a computable two-law width obstruction. They do not by themselves establish the sharper uniform ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\): the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can be bounded at an isolated thin site. Nor does the displayed two-law argument turn score-law total variation alone into an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion without a same-class outcome perturbation whose full observed-law distance is controlled. This is a partial resolution of the honest-adaptation question.

\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(\gamma\) is also smaller than one quarter of the universal numerical risk constant furnished by \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
If \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the same lower bound.  Thus the displayed band attains the matched global expected-sup half-width frontier on the pervasive class and, when that subclass is nonempty, on the base class.

Independently of the preceding small-\(\gamma\) restriction, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
The sharper pointwise ratio to \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\), its matching ratio lower bound, and an exact score-law necessary-and-sufficient criterion are not asserted: the global calibration uses \(\log M_n\asymp\log n\), whereas \(\log\{eK_P(x,h)/\gamma\}\) can remain bounded at an isolated thin site, and score-law total variation alone does not control the distance between full observed laws.

\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  If \(\gamma\) is also smaller than one quarter of the universal numerical risk constant furnished by \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), there is \(c_\gamma>0\), independent of \(n\), such that every data-measurable band sequence with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \ge c_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
If \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\), every band honest over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) obeys the same lower bound. Independently of the preceding small-\(\gamma\) restriction, for any \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing two laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
 \left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
 \operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]

proposed.statement: For a declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), does there exist a data-measurable band \(\mathcal C_n\) such that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma-o(1)\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=O(1)\)? Prove the matching honest-width lower bound: every band sequence satisfying the displayed coverage condition obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\ge c\) for a universal \(c>0\). If the upper target is impossible, characterize exactly which pairs \((\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\) and \((\kappa',\mathsf J'_{-},\mathsf J'_{+})\) in \(\Lambda_n\), separated by their \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) benchmark functions, must satisfy uniform score-law distinguishability \(\inf_{P,P'}\operatorname{TV}(P_X^{\otimes n},(P'_X)^{\otimes n})\to1\), where \(P\) and \(P'\) range over the corresponding two profile-restricted component classes.
proposed.justification: The quantified target separates coverage, local oracle width, and the score-law information needed to decide which thickness profile generated the data.
proposed.gap: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance proves Gaussian uniform bands under positive density and stable Gram matrices; Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm proposes an unknown-density inhomogeneous band but maintains a positive continuous univariate design density; ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands allows data-selected resolutions but does not verify vanishing two-sided boundary information; and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest treats scalar honest intervals.
proposed.consumer: The Ser Pilo Paga replication and companion software can report wider intervals only where the score design is thin while retaining a boundary-wide coverage guarantee.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The displayed inclusion and matched rate expose an internal limitation of the frozen arbitrary-modulus OEQ lower-profile-only exact-characterization demand for the two-argument class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\): matching same-class bounds cannot recover the isolated polynomial frontier when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) declares one thin site, because the class still retains the pervasive subclass. This is a limitation of that class parameterization, not a refutation of any published estimator or workflow. An arbitrary-modulus formulation that separates isolated from pervasive thinning must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile.
proposed.justification: The theorem gives an explicit same-class certificate that a constant lower packing declaration may still contain pervasive thinning and therefore inherit its logarithmic minimax rate.
proposed.gap: A refined class with both lower and upper packing control is required before an exact arbitrary-profile frontier can distinguish isolated thinning.
proposed.consumer: A constant lower packing certificate must not be interpreted as evidence for the isolated rate without a compatible upper-profile certificate.

Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), use the circular inside--outside assignment and constants certified by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), and suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\).  Put \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare
\[
 \mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=\mathbf 1\{u\ge C_mh^\kappa\},
 \qquad 0<h\le h_0,\quad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\cup
 \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \subseteq \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
\]
and there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 \le R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}
 \le C\,r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 {r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{oeq:arbitrary\text{-}modulus\text{-}frontier}\) has a negative answer as stated: a class constrained only by a lower mass modulus and a lower thin-site packing declaration cannot both retain the pervasive subclass and recover the isolated polynomial frontier when the declared multiplicity is one.  To formulate an arbitrary-modulus result that distinguishes the two regimes, one must add an upper thin-site packing restriction or use an intrinsic two-sided profile; under the frozen two-argument class, the requested package of conclusions cannot hold.

\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),

\]

\[

\]
Fix an admissible \(\kappa\).  For every fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_\gamma<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)
 \le C_\gamma(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
\]

Uniform local-oracle width achievability over an arbitrary triangular union, the corresponding local-ratio converse for unions without a nonempty pervasive component, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient criterion stated only through score-law total variation remain open. changed.from:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).
changed.to:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), define \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\), and let \(\mathsf R_P\) and \(N_{t,P}\) be the conditional outcome kernel and side-specific null sets furnished by that assumption. For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\); in particular, all these conclusions hold \(\mu_{t,P}\)-almost everywhere on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\).
